# Available Tools

<!-- Code generated by `go generate ./...`. DO NOT EDIT. -->
<!-- Edit the tool definitions in pkg/toolsets/**/tools.go and regenerate. -->

Each tool is exposed through the MCP protocol and can be invoked by the Rancher AI agent. Tools are grouped by toolset. Tools marked **Write** modify state and are only registered when the server is not running in read-only mode.

## fleet

| Tool | Access | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `analyzeFleetResources` | Read-only | Analyze Fleet resources and diagnose bundle deployment issues.<br><br>This command collects diagnostic information about Fleet resources including GitRepos,<br>Bundles, BundleDeployments, and related resources. It outputs JSON containing only the<br>fields relevant for troubleshooting, making it easy to identify issues like:<br><br>- Bundles stuck with old commits or forceSyncGeneration<br>- BundleDeployments not applying their target deploymentID<br>- Orphaned secrets with invalid owner references<br>- Resources stuck with deletion timestamps due to finalizers<br>- API server consistency issues (time travel)<br>- Missing or problematic Content resources |
| `getBundle` | Read-only | Get a specific Fleet Bundle by name and workspace. |
| `getGitRepo` | Read-only | Get a specific GitRepo by name and workspace. |
| `listGitRepos` | Read-only | List all GitRepos in a workspace. |

## provisioning

| Tool | Access | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `analyzeCluster` | Read-only | Returns cluster configuration and status, including provisioning and management clusters, the CAPI cluster, and machine-pool configs. Optionally include CAPI MachineDeployments, MachineSets, and/or Machines with the corresponding include flags. Use for a cluster-wide overview. Use analyzeClusterMachines or getClusterMachine for focused machine inspection. |
| `analyzeClusterMachines` | Read-only | Lists selected CAPI MachineDeployments, MachineSets, and/or Machines for a cluster. Set at least one include flag. Use when the machine name is unknown or an issue spans multiple machines; use getClusterMachine for a known machine. |
| `createCustomCluster` | Write | Creates a custom cluster within Rancher.<br>This should only be used when the user wants to create a new custom cluster. Do not use this tool if a user asks to create an imported cluster. |
| `createCustomClusterPlan` | Write | Plans to create a custom cluster within Rancher. It returns the JSON representation of the resource to be created without actually creating it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation.<br>This should only be used when the user wants to create a new custom cluster. Do not use this tool if a user asks to create an imported cluster. |
| `createImportedCluster` | Write | Creates an imported cluster within Rancher.<br>This should only be used when the user wants to create a new imported cluster. Do not use this tool when the user asks to create a new custom cluster. |
| `createImportedClusterPlan` | Write | Plans to create an imported cluster within Rancher. It returns the JSON representation of the resource to be created without actually creating it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation.<br>This should only be used when the user wants to create a new imported cluster. Do not use this tool when the user asks to create a new custom cluster. |
| `createK3kCluster` | Write | Create a new K3k cluster in a specific downstream cluster. |
| `createK3kClusterPlan` | Write | Plans to create a new K3k cluster in a specific downstream cluster. It returns the JSON representation of the resource to be created without actually creating it. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `getClusterAutoscaling` | Read-only | Returns whether cluster autoscaling is supported, enabled and paused for an rke2 or k3s cluster, the state of the cluster-autoscaler deployment, and the autoscaling configuration (current size, minimum and maximum size) of each node pool, with a warning for node pools with an incomplete configuration.<br>This should be used when the user wants to know if a cluster has the autoscaler enabled, or before changing the size or autoscaling configuration of a node pool.<br>Autoscaling is only supported for clusters provisioned by Rancher with machine pools; it is not supported for the local cluster, or for custom, imported or k3k clusters. |
| `getClusterMachine` | Read-only | Gets a specific CAPI machine and optionally its owning MachineSet and MachineDeployment. Set at least one include flag. Use when the machine name is known. Use analyzeClusterMachines for issues spanning multiple machines. |
| `listK3kClusters` | Read-only | List K3k virtual clusters deployed across downstream clusters. |
| `listSupportedKubernetesVersions` | Read-only | Returns the currently supported rke2 and k3s versions that can be provisioned.<br>This should only be used when information about the supported rke2 and k3s is needed. This is often required to support provisioning custom and imported clusters. |
| `scaleClusterNodePool` | Write | Changes the size of an existing node pool for an rke2 or k3s cluster.<br>This should be used when the user wants to change the size of an existing node pool for an rke2 or k3s cluster.<br>Pools cannot be scaled to zero nodes, and etcd node pools cannot be scaled below 3 nodes to prevent loss of quorum.<br>Node pools managed by the cluster autoscaler cannot be scaled manually; use updateNodePoolAutoscaling to change their minimum and maximum size instead.<br>The local cluster does not support node pool scaling. |
| `scaleClusterNodePoolPlan` | Write | Plans to change the size of an existing node pool for an rke2 or k3s cluster. It returns the JSON representation of the updated node pool resource without actually applying the change in the cluster.<br>Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. This should be used when the user wants to change the size of an existing node pool for an rke2 or k3s cluster.<br>Pools cannot be scaled to zero nodes, and etcd node pools cannot be scaled below 3 nodes to prevent loss of quorum.<br>Node pools managed by the cluster autoscaler cannot be scaled manually; use updateNodePoolAutoscalingPlan to change their minimum and maximum size instead.<br>The local cluster does not support node pool scaling. |
| `updateNodePoolAutoscaling` | Write | Enables, changes or disables cluster autoscaling for an existing node pool of an rke2 or k3s cluster, by setting the minimum and maximum number of nodes the cluster autoscaler can scale the node pool to.<br>This should be used when the user wants to enable, adjust or disable the autoscaler for a node pool. Use getClusterAutoscaling first to see the current autoscaling configuration.<br>If the current size of the node pool is outside the new range, the node pool is resized to the nearest bound. The minimum size must be at least 1.<br>The response includes a note if the cluster-autoscaling feature is disabled in Rancher or the autoscaler is paused for the cluster, as the node pool won't be scaled until then.<br>Autoscaling is not supported for etcd node pools, as it could leave the cluster with an even number of etcd nodes. The local cluster does not support autoscaling. |
| `updateNodePoolAutoscalingPlan` | Write | Plans to enable, change or disable cluster autoscaling for an existing node pool of an rke2 or k3s cluster. It returns the JSON patch for the cluster without actually applying the change in the cluster.<br>Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. This should be used when the user wants to enable, adjust or disable the autoscaler for a node pool.<br>If the current size of the node pool is outside the new range, the node pool is resized to the nearest bound. The minimum size must be at least 1.<br>Autoscaling is not supported for etcd node pools, as it could leave the cluster with an even number of etcd nodes. The local cluster does not support autoscaling. |

## rancher

| Tool | Access | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `auditInactiveUsers` | Read-only | Audit Rancher users and report those who have not logged in or used a token for at least inactiveDays days, e.g. 90 for 3 months.<br>A user is active if they have logged in or used a token (an API key, kubeconfig or session) since the cutoff; activeByTokenUse counts users who are only active through tokens.<br>A user is inactive if their last login is before the cutoff, or if they have never logged in and their account was created before the cutoff, and they have not used a token since.<br>Users created after the cutoff who have never logged in are not inactive, and are counted in recentlyCreatedNoLogin.<br>System accounts are not audited. Users whose last login cannot be read are listed in undeterminedUsers.<br>Inactive users are sorted by how long they have been inactive, longest first, and include their direct and group global roles, so inactive administrators stand out.<br>activeByTokenUseUsers lists the users who have not logged in since the cutoff but have used a token since, with their last login and last token use.<br>When asked who has not logged in, as opposed to who is inactive, report inactiveUsers and activeByTokenUseUsers, saying that the latter still use tokens.<br>Counts cover every user checked, not only the returned page. Already-disabled accounts are included and counted in alreadyDisabled.<br>Always pass on the caveat in notes: deleted tokens leave no record, or, if includeTokenActivity is false, token use is not counted at all.<br>If visibility is limited, only the caller's own user or tokens could be read, so do not conclude that no users are inactive. |
| `createGlobalRole` | Write | Creates a global role in Rancher.<br>Rules grant permissions in the local cluster where Rancher runs.<br>Inherited cluster roles grant the named cluster role templates in every downstream cluster.<br>Use createGlobalRoleBinding to assign the global role to users or groups. |
| `createGlobalRoleBinding` | Write | Assigns a global role to a user or group by creating a global role binding (GRB).<br>Exactly one of user or group must be specified. The user can be a username or user ID.<br>The global role must be specified by name. Use getGlobalRole to find the name from a display name. |
| `createGlobalRoleBindingPlan` | Write | Plans to assign a global role to a user or group. It returns the JSON representation of the global role binding to be created without actually creating it. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `createGlobalRolePlan` | Write | Plans to create a global role in Rancher. It returns the JSON representation of the global role to be created without actually creating it. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `createKubernetesResource` | Write | Creates a resource in a Kubernetes cluster from a complete Kubernetes manifest passed in the 'manifest' field, in YAML or JSON. The namespace must be empty for cluster-wide resources.<br><br>Example of the manifest parameter (YAML):<br>apiVersion: v1<br>kind: ConfigMap<br>metadata:<br>name: my-cm<br>data:<br>key: value |
| `createKubernetesResourcePlan` | Write | Plans to create a resource in a Kubernetes cluster from a complete Kubernetes manifest passed in the 'manifest' field, in YAML or JSON. It returns the JSON representation of the resource to be created without actually creating it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. The namespace must be empty for cluster-wide resources. |
| `createProject` | Write | Creates a project resource for a specified cluster with the given containerResourceQuota. |
| `createProjectPlan` | Write | Plans to create a project resource for a specified cluster. It returns the JSON representation of the project to be created without actually creating it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `createProjectRoleTemplateBinding` | Write | Grants a user or group a role in a project by creating a project role template binding (PRTB), e.g. to add a project member.<br>Common project roles are project-owner, project-member and read-only. Defaults to project-member.<br>If the user or group already has the role in the project, no changes are made. |
| `createProjectRoleTemplateBindingPlan` | Write | Plans to grant a user or group a role in a project. It returns the JSON representation of the project role template binding (PRTB) to be created without actually creating it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `deleteGlobalRole` | Write | Deletes a global role by name. Built-in global roles cannot be deleted.<br>Rancher also deletes every global role binding (GRB) for the global role, so all users and groups assigned the role lose it.<br>Use getGlobalRole to find the name from a display name. |
| `deleteGlobalRoleBinding` | Write | Removes a global role from a user or group by deleting the global role binding (GRB) with the given name.<br>Use listGlobalRoleBindings to find the name of the binding to delete. |
| `deleteGlobalRoleBindingPlan` | Write | Plans to remove a global role from a user or group. It returns the JSON representation of the global role binding to be deleted without actually deleting it. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `deleteGlobalRolePlan` | Write | Plans to delete a global role. It returns the JSON representation of the global role to be deleted without actually deleting it, with a caution giving the number of users and groups bound to the global role. Only used for displaying the resource when using human validation. |
| `getClusterImages` | Read-only | Returns all container images running across the specified clusters, along with the pods (name and namespace) using each image. Use in priority this tool to audit clusters for container registry or image usage, or to find which pods are running a specific container image. If clusters is empty, returns data for all clusters. |
| `getClusterResourceUsage` | Read-only | Returns the overall resource usage of a cluster, as totals for the entire cluster as well as broken down by node.<br>For CPU, memory and pods it includes the capacity and allocatable resources of the nodes, the requests and limits of the pods scheduled on them, and the actual usage when the metrics server is available, with percentages relative to the allocatable resources.<br>If node metrics can't be retrieved, metricsUnavailableReason explains why, e.g. because the user isn't allowed to read metrics or the metrics server isn't installed.<br>Nodes without metrics, such as nodes that have just joined or are not ready, are listed in nodesWithoutMetrics, and cluster-wide actual usage is then omitted because it would be understated.<br>It also reports the number of ready nodes and the number of pending pods that could not be scheduled, which indicates that the cluster is running out of capacity.<br>Use this tool to check how much of a cluster's capacity is used, or whether a cluster needs to be scaled. |
| `getCurrentUser` | Read-only | Get the Rancher user that owns the credentials used to call Rancher. Use this to answer "who am I?".<br>Returns the user ID, login name, the principal IDs Rancher reports for the token and their providers (principalProviders, e.g. local, openldap, github), and group principals.<br>The login name and principals come from Rancher's view of the token, so they can differ from the username on the User resource and from how the token was issued.<br>To find every provider the user can log in with, use getUser with the returned user ID and read its authProviders.<br>getUser can also find the user by the returned login name, even when it is a provider username such as an email address.<br>When the MCP server is configured with a fixed token this is the owner of that token, which may not be the person asking.<br>Use getUser with the returned user ID for more details about the user. |
| `getDeployment` | Read-only | Returns a Deployment and its Pods. It must be used for troubleshooting problems with deployments. |
| `getGlobalRole` | Read-only | Get a global role by name or display name, including the rules and inherited cluster roles that define its permissions.<br>Names and display names are matched case-insensitively. If more than one global role matches, all of them are returned.<br>If no global role matches, the names and display names of all global roles are returned so the closest one can be suggested. |
| `getKubernetesResource` | Read-only | Fetches a Kubernetes resource from the cluster. The namespace must be empty for all namespaces or cluster-wide resources. |
| `getNodeMetrics` | Read-only | Returns a list of all nodes in a specified Kubernetes cluster, including their current resource utilization metrics. |
| `getProject` | Read-only | Returns a project resource and its associated namespaces and members. |
| `getResourceUsage` | Read-only | Returns the resource usage for a namespace, project or all projects in a cluster.<br>Usage totals are provided for the entire project as well as broken down by namespace.<br>The resource usage includes CPU and memory requests, limits and actual usage, as well as the total number of pods. |
| `getRoleTemplate` | Read-only | Get a role template by name. |
| `getUser` | Read-only | Get a user by user ID, login name, display name, principal ID, or the username they log in with at an external provider,<br>e.g. "u-abc12", "admin", "Jo Smith", "openldap_user://uid=jo,dc=example,dc=org" or "jo@example.com".<br>Display names and provider usernames are matched case-insensitively. Users from external providers often have no login name,<br>so find them by provider username (such as the email address they log in to an OIDC provider with), display name or principal ID.<br>Every matching user is returned. If more than one matches, ask which one is meant.<br>Returns the user ID, login name, display name, the authentication providers the user can log in with (authProviders),<br>whether the account is enabled, when it was created, when the user last logged in, the global roles bound directly to the user,<br>the groups the user belongs to (groups), the global roles they have through those groups (groupGlobalRoles),<br>and the username they log in with at each external provider (providerUsernames).<br>authProviders includes local only for users with a login name, since users created by an external provider have no local password.<br>It does not check whether each provider is enabled, use listAuthProviders for that. System accounts have no authProviders.<br>groups and providerUsernames are as Rancher recorded them when the user last logged in, or last refreshed their groups.<br>Report both directGlobalRoles and groupGlobalRoles when describing what a user can do: administrators often get admin through a group.<br>lastLogin.state is one of recorded, noLoginRecorded, unknown, or notApplicable for system accounts.<br>Using an API token does not count as a login, so a user who only uses API tokens can look inactive.<br>unavailableFields lists information the credentials are not allowed to read. |
| `inspectPod` | Read-only | Returns all information related to a Pod. It includes its parent Deployment or StatefulSet, the CPU and memory consumption and the logs. It must be used for troubleshooting problems with pods. |
| `listAuthProviders` | Read-only | List the authentication providers enabled in Rancher, e.g. local, keycloakoidc, openldap, activedirectory or github.<br>Use this to answer which authentication mechanisms are active, or how users can log in.<br>Each provider's name is also the prefix of its users' principal IDs, e.g. keycloakoidc_user://.<br>Works for every user, without needing permission to read Rancher's auth configuration. |
| `listClusterRoleTemplateBindings` | Read-only | List all cluster role template bindings (CRTBs) in a Rancher cluster.<br>If a user is specified only returns CRTBs for that user and the groups the user belongs to.<br>If a group is specified only returns CRTBs for that group. A user and a group cannot both be specified.<br>CRTBs provide users permissions as specified by a RoleTemplate at the cluster level. |
| `listGlobalRoleBindings` | Read-only | List all global role bindings (GRBs) in Rancher.<br>If a user is specified only returns GRBs for that user and the groups the user belongs to.<br>If a group is specified only returns GRBs for that group. A user and a group cannot both be specified.<br>If a global role is specified only returns GRBs for that global role.<br>GRBs provide users or groups permissions as specified by a GlobalRole across Rancher.<br>To find out everything a user can do, combine GRBs with their cluster and project role template bindings. |
| `listGlobalRoles` | Read-only | List all global roles in Rancher.<br>Global roles define permissions that apply across Rancher rather than to a specific cluster or project. |
| `listKubernetesResources` | Read-only | Returns a list of Kubernetes resources. The namespace must be empty for all namespaces or cluster-wide resources. Supports an optional JSONPath predicate to filter which resources are returned.<br><br>Results are paginated with limit (page size, default 100) and offset (how many resources to skip from the start, default 0). To page through results, keep limit the same and increase offset by limit each time: offset=0 is the first page, offset=100 is the second page, offset=200 is the third page, and so on (with limit=100). When more resources remain, the response includes the exact offset value to pass in for the next page. |
| `listProjectRoleTemplateBindings` | Read-only | List all project role template bindings (PRTBs) in a Rancher cluster.<br>If a user is specified only returns PRTBs for that user and the groups the user belongs to.<br>If a group is specified only returns PRTBs for that group. A user and a group cannot both be specified.<br>If a project ID is specified only returns PRTBs for that project.<br>PRTBs provide users permissions as specified by a RoleTemplate in a project. |
| `listProjects` | Read-only | Returns a list of project resources for a specified cluster. |
| `listRoleTemplates` | Read-only | List all role templates in a Rancher cluster.<br>Role templates define a set of permissions that can be assigned to users or groups. |
| `listTokenUsage` | Read-only | Report the tokens each user has and when each was last used, from both the v3 tokens and the newer ext.cattle.io tokens.<br>Use this to find out whether a user or automation account is active through API keys or kubeconfigs, since using a token does not count as a login.<br>Each token has a type (session for logins, apiKey for API keys, or another kind such as kubeconfig), when it expires, whether it has expired, and when it was last used.<br>Users are sorted by their most recent token use. Expired tokens are counted but only listed if includeExpired is set. Token values are never returned.<br>If visibility is limited, only the caller's own tokens are included, so do not conclude that other users have no tokens. |
| `listUsers` | Read-only | List Rancher users, with the same summary of each user as getUser, except that the groups each user belongs to are left out<br>to keep the list short. groupGlobalRoles is still included, so users who are administrators through a group stand out; use getUser for a user's groups.<br>System accounts that Rancher creates for itself are left out and counted in systemAccountsExcluded, unless includeSystemAccounts is set.<br>total is the number of users across all pages. Results are paginated with limit and offset.<br>If visibility is limited, the credentials are not allowed to list users and only the caller's own user is included, so do not<br>conclude that no other users exist. |
| `moveNamespace` | Write | Moves a namespace to a project in the specified cluster. |
| `moveNamespacePlan` | Write | Plans to move a namespace to a project in the specified cluster. It returns the original namespace, the JSON patch and the patched namespace that would be applied without actually applying it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the change when using human validation. |
| `patchKubernetesResource` | Write | Patches a Kubernetes resource using a JSON patch. Don't ask for confirmation. The namespace must be empty for cluster-wide resources. The content type used is application/json-patch+json. Returns the modified resource. |
| `patchKubernetesResourcePlan` | Write | Plans to patch a Kubernetes resource using a JSON patch. It returns the JSON representation of the planned update without actually applying it in the cluster. Only used for displaying the patch when using human validation. The namespace must be empty for cluster-wide resources. The content type used is application/json-patch+json. |

## rancher,provisioning

| Tool | Access | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `listClusters` | Read-only | Returns a list of all Rancher clusters, including local and downstream clusters. |
